claim.pdf_says:
7.3.8.4.2 General format

compilation-variable-name-1 IS [ NOT ] DEFINED

(printed with NOT and DEFINED UNDERLINED; IS is printed WITHOUT an underline; compilation-variable-name-1 is a lowercase generic term)
claim.markdown_says:
#### 7.3.8.4.2 General format

compilation-variable-name-1 IS [ NOT ] DEFINED

(plain text; no underline markup, and no "Figure notes" blockquote recording which words are underlined -- unlike every other general format in the surrounding clause range, e.g. 7.3.4 CALL-CONVENTION, 7.3.10 DEFINE, 7.3.24 SOURCE FORMAT, which all carry a Figure notes block naming the underlined words)
claim.why_it_matters: Per the notation convention the document itself transcribes at ISO_COBOL.md line 5805 -- 'Within each format, uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words and may be specified at the user's option with no effect on the semantics of the format' -- IS is an OPTIONAL word here. 'compilation-variable-name-1 DEFINED' and 'compilation-variable-name-1 NOT DEFINED' are legal defined conditions with IS omitted. The flattened markdown makes IS look mandatory: the exact falsely-restrictive-syntax failure mode this sweep targets. It also loses that NOT and DEFINED are required keywords. This is the only general format on pages 75-88 that carries any underlining, and the only one in this range with no Figure notes block.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by direct glyph inspection of the 300-dpi render (E:/Temp/specrecon/v88/spec_p88.png, cropped and 3x-upscaled to E:/Temp/specrecon/v88/fmt_zoom.png). The printed general format line under 7.3.8.4.2 reads: compilation-variable-name-1 IS [ NOT ] DEFINED. At the glyph level the underline rule runs beneath N-O-T only (starting under the N, ending under the T, NOT extending under the enclosing square brackets) and beneath D-E-F-I-N-E-D in full. There is unambiguously NO rule beneath 'IS' -- the baseline under I and S is clean white, and the nearest underline segment begins well to the right, after the opening bracket. compilation-variable-name-1 is lowercase and not underlined. So the PDF is quoted exactly right.

The markdown is also quoted exactly right. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 3876 is the heading '#### 7.3.8.4.2 General format' and line 3878 is the bare plain-text line 'compilation-variable-name-1 IS [ NOT ] DEFINED'. I read the master file directly (lines 3860-3900), not just the page-88 work-unit extract, to rule out the extract being lossy: there is no code fence, no underline markup of any kind, and no '> **Figure notes ...**' blockquote anywhere in clause 7.3.8.4.

I tried to refute this three ways and could not.

(1) 'It is only formatting.' It is not. In an ISO COBOL general format, underlining is the meta-language that separates required words from optional words -- 8.3.2.4.3, which the transcription itself carries at ISO_COBOL.md line 5805, states verbatim: 'Within each format, uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words and may be specified at the user's option with no effect on the semantics of the format.' The claim's quotation of that line is accurate. Because IS is uppercase and unruled, IS is an optional word, and 'compilation-variable-name-1 DEFINED' / 'compilation-variable-name-1 NOT DEFINED' are legal defined conditions. Nothing in the flattened markdown conveys that, and general rules 1 and 2 (lines 3888/3890) actively push the reader the other way by naming the constructs 'the IS DEFINED syntax' and 'the IS NOT DEFINED syntax'. An implementer working from the markdown would reject legal source -- the falsely-restrictive-syntax failure mode.

(2) 'The information survives elsewhere in the document.' It does not. Grepping every occurrence of compilation-variable-name-1 and of 'defined condition' across ISO_COBOL.md turns up no other rendering of this format and no statement that IS is optional here. The loss is total and unrecoverable from the markdown alone.

(3) 'The transcription simply does not record underlining.' It does, systematically -- there are 225 '**Figure notes ...**' blockquotes in ISO_COBOL.md that enumerate underlined words, and the directly analogous case is handled correctly: line 4871, SOURCE FORMAT, reads '`SOURCE`, `FIXED`, and `FREE` are underlined in the printed standard (required words). `FORMAT` and `IS` are **not** underlined -- they are optional words.' That is the same optional-IS distinction, recorded there and dropped here. So this is an omission against the transcription's own established convention, not a convention that simply does not exist.

I also checked the other apparent divergence on this page and rejected it: the run-over sentence 'binary value of each character's encoding is used. If the literals are of unequal length they are not equal.' is absent from the page-88 slice but present at ISO_COBOL.md line 3858, merged into its parent item 2) on page 87. That is ordinary page-break furniture, not a defect.

What the claim got wrong is only its supporting colour, not its substance -- see corrected_description.
verdict.corrected_description:
REAL, normative -- but two supporting assertions in the claim are false and should not be repeated in the ledger.

The genuine defect: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 3878 transcribes the 7.3.8.4.2 (Defined condition) general format as undifferentiated plain text, 'compilation-variable-name-1 IS [ NOT ] DEFINED', discarding the printed underlining. In the PDF, NOT and DEFINED are underlined (required words) and IS is printed without an underline, making IS an optional word under 8.3.2.4.3 (ISO_COBOL.md line 5805). The markdown therefore loses the fact that 'compilation-variable-name-1 DEFINED' and 'compilation-variable-name-1 NOT DEFINED' are legal, and loses that NOT and DEFINED are the required keywords. Clause 7.3.8.4 carries no 'Figure notes' blockquote, so the distinction is recoverable nowhere in the markdown. The fix is a Figure notes block in the house style, e.g.: '> **Figure notes (defined condition general format).** `NOT` and `DEFINED` are underlined in the printed standard (required words). `IS` is **not** underlined -- it is an optional word and may be omitted. The brackets around `NOT` are not underlined and make the negation optional.' This exactly parallels the existing SOURCE FORMAT note at line 4871.

Correction 1 -- 'the only general format on pages 75-88 that carries any underlining' is FALSE. Pages 75-88 contain the COPY statement general format (page 76, line 3394) and the REPLACE Format 1 syntax diagram (page 80, line 3535), both of which carry extensive underlining in the printed standard.

Correction 2 -- 'the only one in this range with no Figure notes block' is FALSE. 7.3.2 General format on page 84 (line 3692) also has no Figure notes block, correctly so: it is the one-token format '>>compiler-instruction', with no underlining and no meta-language to record. Within pages 75-88 the accurate statement is that COPY (Figure notes at line 3407) and REPLACE (line 3545) both carry their notes, and 7.3.8.4.2 is the sole format in the range with printed underlining that has none.

Neither correction weakens the finding; the surrounding-clause precedents the claim cites -- CALL-CONVENTION (line 3920), DEFINE (line 4028), SOURCE FORMAT (line 4871) -- all exist and all carry Figure notes as described.
